title: Lipschitz AP-Free Graphs
exact_target: Can an integer-valued function with a fixed bound on its slope have a graph containing no three equally spaced collinear graph points? Equivalently, can an increasing integer sequence with bounded gaps avoid every progression in which both the indices and the values form three-term arithmetic progressions?

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, \emph{UnsolvedMath: A Curated Collection of Open Mathematics Problems}, record 104 (GREEN-015). CC BY 4.0.

Tom Brown, Veselin Jungić and Andrew Poelstra, \emph{On Double 3-Term Arithmetic Progressions}, arXiv:1304.1829v3, 16 November 2013, section 1, Conjecture 1 and Problem 1, pp. 1--3, giving the equivalent bounded-gap and additive-square formulations. The existence question here is the negation of the universal question in Problem 1.
Ben Green, \emph{100 Open Problems}, author manuscript with December 2025 updates, Problem 15, p. 10.
